To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the radiolarian assembages in the Japan Sea have changed significantly during the last 200 kyrs, which may be related to changes in the hydrography of the Japan Sea.

the assemblage composition of radiolarians in the Japan Sea has changed significantly during the last 250 kyrs, reflecting the variations of surface and deep-water environments, as well as the inflow of the Tsushima Current.

the radiolarian species abundance changes during the last 200 kyrs in the Sea of Japan are related to the variations in the Tsushima Warm current and the deep water circulation, and the millennial-scale variations in radiolarian assembalges are related to the Dansgaard-Oescher cycles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between the radiolarian assemblages and the environmental changes of the Japan Sea during the last 200 kyrs.
the response of radiolarians to the orbital-scale and millennial-scale climatic changes in the Japan Sea during the last 200 kyrs.
the response of radiolarian species assemblages to changes in sea surface conditions, deep-water oxygen content, and organic fluxes in the Japan Sea during the last 210,000 years.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
radiolarian assemblages in the Japan Sea have been controlled by the inflow of the Tsushima Current, salinity of surface waters and ventilation of deep water.

the radiolarian assemblage in the Japan Sea is strongly affected by the changes of the Tsushima and Oyashio currents, and also by changes in salinity of surface water, oxygen content of deep water, and organic flux.

the changes of radiolaria abundance are mainly caused by changes in the inflows of the Kuroshio Current and the Tsushima Warm current, and also by the variations in the oxygen content of deep water and organic matter flux.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the radiolarian assemblage changes during the last 200 kyrs in this region are controlled primarily by the changes of the Tsushima Current, and secondarily by the inflow of oxygen and organic material into deeper water.
changes in the abundance of the above-mentioned seven radiolarian taxa were mainly controlled by the inflow/outflow of the Tsushima Current and by the oxygenation of deep-water.

changes in the radiolarian assembles were controlled by the inflows of the warm Tsushima Warm Current during the interglacial period and the isolation of the Japan Sea from the surrounding seas during glacial periods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the abundance of the radiolarian species can be useful for the reconstruction of paleoenvironment in the Japan Sea and the adjacent seas.
the abundance of seven radiolaria species changed significantly during the last 210 ka, and these changes were probably related to changes in oceanographic conditions.
